ports.title: SSH service exposed on TCP/22
ports.description: SSH is reachable on TCP port 22.
ports.possible_attack: An attacker with network access could attempt unauthorized SSH authentication.
ports.why_it_matters: SSH provides remote administration, so unnecessary exposure increases the reachable attack surface.
ports.how_to_defend: Use strong authentication or SSH keys, restrict trusted source addresses, disable unnecessary remote access, and keep SSH updated.

ports.title: Telnet service exposed on TCP/23
ports.description: Telnet is reachable on TCP port 23.
ports.possible_attack: An attacker with network access could attempt unauthorized remote access or observe unencrypted Telnet communication.
ports.why_it_matters: Telnet does not provide modern protection for remote-administration traffic.
ports.how_to_defend: Disable Telnet and use SSH instead. Restrict remote administration to trusted systems.

ports.title: DNS service exposed on TCP/53
ports.description: DNS is reachable on TCP port 53.
ports.possible_attack: An attacker could interact with an exposed DNS service and investigate configuration weaknesses.
ports.why_it_matters: Incorrectly configured DNS can disclose network information or provide unintended functionality.
ports.how_to_defend: Restrict DNS queries and zone transfers to trusted systems and keep the DNS service updated.

ports.title: HTTP service exposed on TCP/80
ports.description: HTTP is reachable on TCP port 80.
ports.possible_attack: An attacker could access the exposed web service and look for weak authentication, unsafe configuration, or outdated software.
ports.why_it_matters: An exposed web service increases the reachable application attack surface.
ports.how_to_defend: Use HTTPS where supported, restrict administration interfaces, remove unnecessary services, use strong authentication, and update the application.

risks.title: SSH service exposed
risks.description: SSH is a legitimate administration service but increases the exposed attack surface.
risks.protection: Restrict SSH to trusted hosts, use strong authentication, and disable unused access.

risks.title: Telnet exposed
risks.description: Telnet transmits communication without modern encryption.
risks.protection: Disable Telnet and use SSH or another encrypted management protocol.

risks.title: HTTP service detected

risks.protection: Prefer HTTPS and redirect HTTP traffic where appropriate.

ports.title: Exposed service on TCP/8443
ports.description: TCP port 8443 is reachable. Review whether this service needs network exposure.
ports.possible_attack: An attacker with network access could investigate the exposed service for authentication or configuration weaknesses.
ports.why_it_matters: Every reachable service increases the network attack surface.
ports.how_to_defend: Disable the service if unnecessary. Otherwise restrict access to trusted hosts, require strong authentication, and keep the software updated.

ports.title: MS RPC service exposed on TCP/135
ports.description: MS RPC is reachable on TCP port 135.
ports.possible_attack: An attacker could investigate exposed Windows RPC functionality from the reachable network.
ports.why_it_matters: RPC is legitimate Windows infrastructure but can increase lateral-movement exposure when unnecessarily reachable.
ports.how_to_defend: Restrict RPC using Windows Firewall and network segmentation and keep Windows security updates current.

ports.title: NetBIOS service exposed on TCP/139
ports.description: NetBIOS is reachable on TCP port 139.
ports.possible_attack: An attacker could investigate exposed legacy Windows file and name-sharing functionality.
ports.why_it_matters: Legacy Windows networking can expose additional network information and services.
ports.how_to_defend: Disable NetBIOS where it is not required and restrict legacy Windows networking traffic.

ports.title: SMB service exposed on TCP/445
ports.description: SMB is reachable on TCP port 445.
ports.possible_attack: An attacker with network access could investigate exposed SMB resources or file-sharing configuration.
ports.why_it_matters: SMB provides network file and resource sharing and can increase lateral-movement exposure.
ports.how_to_defend: Restrict SMB to trusted systems, disable unnecessary file sharing, disable SMBv1, use strong authentication, and keep the system updated.

ports.title: MySQL service exposed on TCP/3306
ports.description: MySQL is reachable on TCP port 3306.
ports.possible_attack: An attacker could attempt unauthorized database authentication against an exposed MySQL service.
ports.why_it_matters: Database services may contain sensitive application data.
ports.how_to_defend: Restrict MySQL to trusted application hosts, use strong authentication, and keep the database updated.
